subject: Operational escape hatch & customer update — Checkoutly latency spike
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability alert — Checkoutly p95 jump (investigating)

Team,

Monitoring flagged a sustained p95 jump for Checkoutly starting ~08:50 PDT. Visible symptoms: 4x p95 increase on gen API (model: redwood-2-8b), tail calls timing out around 3% of requests, small drop in throughput as retries increased. I'm already running the dashboards and attaching the immediate p95 snapshot (p95_trend_0714.png).

First pass checks:
- No obvious infra scaling failures on the Dedicated pool assigned to the account.
- KV cache miss rate increased for the Checkoutly keyspace (~18% -> 46%).
- A spike in long-sequence requests (avg seq len +60%) correlates with start time.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben — can you confirm whether any kernel/driver logs show GPU stalls in the affected hosts?
2) Marissa — we should scope product-level mitigations (short-term routing or QoS) and what we want to tell the customer.
3) Jonas/Aisha — prep a one-paragraph customer-facing note we can send after we have a safe short-term mitigation.

My initial mitigation idea: a conservative escape hatch that routes Checkoutly traffic to a lower-memory model variant (redwood-2-4b-quant) for requests where sequence length > 1024 (detectable at router) OR when tail latency passes 1.2s. This preserves throughput and avoids long kv-cache churn. Ben, how risky is a live routing rule like that?

I'll loop in more diagnostic logs as I have them.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability alert — Checkoutly p95 jump (investigating)

Soojin,

I've pulled kernel and host-level logs for the dedicated pool. Quick summary:
- No OOMs or node reboots.
- We are seeing periodic SM stalls on two GPUs in pool-us-west-2c that coincide with the spike window; driver traces show long memcpy stalls for large attention caches (~78ms events).
- CUDA driver versions are identical across pool; hardware thermal throttling is not flagged.

Routing to a smaller quantized variant is feasible and the safest quick win. Implementation notes:
- We can add a temporary route with two checks: (1) request.num_input_tokens > 1024 OR (2) realtime p95(30s) > 1.2s. The routing layer supports both predicates.
- We'll deploy the rule in staging for 20m smoke, then push to prod with a 10% ramp, and kill the rule if we see >2% error delta.
- Risk: model-quality regressions for long-sequence completions; hold product/PM to decide whether to apply only to stateless generate endpoints or to chat flows as well.

I've attached a short-run mitigation draft (temp-routing-hack.md) with the exact rollout steps.

Ben Carter
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability alert — Checkoutly p95 jump (investigating)

Thanks — good diagnosis. A few product asks before we flip anything:

1) Scope: prefer we limit the escape hatch to the generation endpoint only (no function calling or tool execution) to reduce regression risk.
2) Telemetry: we need to tag routed requests so we can compare end-to-end quality against a prompt-sample set (I'll attach a minimal eval set in a follow-up if we go live).
3) Customer messaging: keep it simple and action-focused. Key points: we're applying a targeted routing rule to stabilize latency, this is temporary, and we'll follow up with quality metrics in 24-48h.

Jonas — please draft the outbound note and include an ETA for a deeper postmortem.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product (Serving)
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Park <emma.park@checkoutly.com>, ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-14T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Stabilizing Checkoutly latency — brief note (draft)

Emma / Checkoutly ops,

Quick update from Redwood: we observed elevated latency for a subset of your traffic this morning. To stabilize performance while we investigate root cause, we are applying a temporary routing rule that will divert long-sequence generation requests to a compact model variant for a short period.

What this means for you:
- Immediate: improved p95 and throughput for affected calls; you should see fewer timeouts and a smoother experience.
- Side effects: very rare changes to output style for very long completions (>1024 tokens). We are restricting the rule to the standard generation endpoint and not to tool/function calls.
- Next steps: our engineering team will monitor the impact closely over the next 24 hours. We will follow up with a short postmortem and a quality comparison for a sample set within 48 hours.

If you prefer that we do not apply the temporary rule, tell us and we can hold off while we complete additional diagnostics (may result in prolonged degraded latency).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachment: customer-brief-draft-jonas.docx
From: Emma Park <emma.park@checkoutly.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@checkoutly.com, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-15T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stabilizing Checkoutly latency — brief note (draft)

Thanks for the transparency. We are OK with the temporary routing rule — priority is to keep the checkout flows stable. A couple of asks:

- Can you confirm whether the rule will apply across our US and EU traffic or be region-limited?
- Please send the quality sample before/after comparison as soon as you have it so we can review regressions.

Appreciate the quick response.

— Emma Park
Head of Product, Checkoutly
